description: The Cycling Infrastructure Database is Transport for London's survey of cycling infrastructure on every street in every London borough, covering 1,595 square kilometres and over 240,000 assets, with 480,000 photographs. It records cycle lanes and tracks (segregated or painted), cycle parking with type and capacity (146,000 spaces), signalised crossings for cycles, modal filters and traffic gates, traffic calming including every speed hump, advanced stop lines, early-release signals, signed routes and wayfinding (2,000 km of routes, 58,000 signs), dismount points, and paths through parks. TfL built it under its Cycling Action Plan; it feeds TfL's Journey Planner and was used for the Cycle Parking Implementation Plan. The data are free GeoJSON files on TfL's cycling open data portal with a schema and asset guide, under the Transport Data Service licence, and an R package (CycleInfraLnd) imports them. The London Datastore lists a monthly update frequency but its entry was last updated over six years ago. Caveats: it is a single-city inventory, currency after the original survey is unclear, and it holds no counts or flows. The database supports network flow and capacity planning for cycling, such as building a cycle network graph for route choice or parking demand models; related records are the Propensity to Cycle Tool and OSMnx.
